label: prf:flavor-mass-splitting-bound
title: Proof of flavor mass splitting bound
html:
Proof sketch

Two ingredients:

  1. Positivity (lower bound). By substrate construction, q > 1 implies (q-1)^2 > 0 and 1 - q^{-4} > 0. Their product is positive; division by 3 preserves the sign. By prop:flavor-dressed-mass-from-substrate-split the splitting \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} is M_N times this positive substrate factor (modulo O((\Delta m / M_N)^2), which is below the leading term), so the difference is strictly positive.

  2. Upper bound. The substrate factor satisfies

    \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
    \;<\;
    \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^2} \cdot (q - q^{-1}) \cdot (q + q^{-1})
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q-1)^2 (q^4 - 1)}{q^4}.

Both expressions share the numerator (q-1)^2; their ratio is

    \frac{(1 - q^{-4}) / 3}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{(q^4 - 1)/(3 q^4)}{(q^4 - 1)/q^4}
    \;=\;
    \frac{1}{3},

The substrate factor of the proposition equals 1/3 of the bound expression. Multiplication by M_N preserves the inequality; the Skein-side adjustment factor (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})/(q + q^{-1}) < 1 at q > 1 tightens the bound further but is not required for the strict inequality. \square

Tightness

The bound is not tight: the slack-ratio identity above shows that the realised splitting is exactly (1/3) \cdot (q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})/(q + q^{-1}) of the bound (plus a small higher-order correction). The dominant factor is the explicit 1/3 baked into the substrate formula of prop:flavor-split-substrate. Tightening would require either:

  • A finer substrate factor that absorbs the 1/3 directly into the categorical derivation (rather than as an artefact of the closed-form algebra).
  • A different categorical bound source (e.g. prop:hecke-convergence-bound applied to the splitting word) — but this requires further development and is not committed in this revision.

Per-flavor bounds (out of scope)

This theorem does not assert per-flavor bounds 0 < \mu_q < c \cdot M_N. Such bounds require additional non-substrate inputs (the nucleon-baryon sum rule for the average \bar\mu) and live in the open follow-up; see rem:dressed-quark-numerology-at-q0.
